question: Which acquirer had the higher first-attempt approval rate on domestic credit cards in Brazil in June 2026, A or C, and by how much?

question: Which Colombian issuer had the highest final approval rate on debit cards in Colombia in July 2026, and by how much did it lead the second?

question: Did the decline-map hotfix of 15 August 2026 bring back Acquirer B's retries of 'do not honor' declines in Mexico?
gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN created_ts_local < TIMESTAMP'2026-08-06 07:00:00' THEN '1: 23 Jul to 6 Aug' WHEN created_ts_local < TIMESTAMP'2026-08-15 07:00:00' THEN '2: 6 to 15 Aug (map v2.3)' ELSE '3: 15 to 29 Aug (map v2.3.1)' END AS period, count(*) AS failed_first_attempts, round(avg(CAST(is_cascaded AS INT)), 4) AS cascade_rate, round(avg(CAST(recovered_by_cascade AS INT)), 4) AS recovery_rate, sum(CAST(recovered_by_cascade AS INT)) AS recovered FROM workspace.approval_copilot.silver_payments WHERE country = 'MX' AND first_acquirer_id = 'B' AND first_iso_code = '05' AND sent_to_acquirer AND NOT first_attempt_approved AND created_ts_local >= TIMESTAMP'2026-07-23 07:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT change_id, changed_at_utc, change_type, scope, description FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_change_log WHERE change_id IN ('CHG-0806', 'CHG-0815')

facts.K1: Yes. From the map change of 6 August (CHG-0806, v2.3) to the hotfix of 15 August (CHG-0815, 13:00 UTC, 07:00 in Mexico City), none of Acquirer B's failed first attempts with 'do not honor' (05) in Mexico were retried on another acquirer (cascade rate 0%, no recoveries). After the hotfix they were retried again, at about 100%, as in the two weeks before 6 August.
facts.K2: The retries recovered payments again at about the earlier rate: about 38% after the hotfix (167 from 15 to 29 August), against about 38.5% in the two weeks before 6 August.
facts.K3: The hotfix (map v2.3.1) reclassified 05 as soft and retryable for Acquirer B, undoing what v2.3 had done.

question: Did the risk-rule tuning of 20 June 2026 bring Brazil's conversion back?
gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN business_date <= DATE'2026-06-17' THEN '1: 4 to 17 Jun' WHEN business_date <= DATE'2026-06-19' THEN '2: 18 and 19 Jun' WHEN business_date = DATE'2026-06-20' THEN '3: 20 Jun' ELSE '4: 21 Jun to 4 Jul' END AS period, sum(payment_intents) AS payment_intents, round(sum(blocked_by_risk) / sum(payment_intents), 4) AS risk_block_rate, round(sum(approved) / sum(payment_intents), 4) AS conversion_rate FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_funnel_daily WHERE country = 'BR' AND business_date BETWEEN DATE'2026-06-04' AND DATE'2026-07-04' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT change_id, changed_at_utc, change_type, scope, description FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_change_log WHERE change_id IN ('CHG-0618', 'CHG-0620')

facts.K1: Yes. After the tuning (risk rules v3.1, CHG-0620, 20 June 18:00 UTC), the share of Brazilian payment intents blocked by risk went back to about its level before 18 June (about 1.3% from 21 June to 4 July, against about 1.25% from 4 to 17 June and about 3.5% on 18 and 19 June), and conversion returned to about 85% (about 85.3%, against 85.0% before and about 82.6% on 18 and 19 June).
facts.K2: The fall came from risk rules v3 (CHG-0618, 18 June), a new card-velocity rule.

question: During the issuer maintenance in Brazil on the morning of 21 July 2026, did retries on another acquirer recover the declined payments?
gold_sql: SELECT issuer_id = 'BR-ISS-03' AS issuer_in_maintenance, CASE WHEN created_ts_local >= TIMESTAMP'2026-07-21 09:00:00' THEN 'window' ELSE 'previous 14 days, same hours' END AS period, count(*) AS payments_sent, round(avg(CAST(final_approved AS INT)), 4) AS final_approval_rate, sum(CAST(NOT first_attempt_approved AS INT)) AS failed_first_attempts, sum(CAST(is_cascaded AS INT)) AS retried, sum(CAST(recovered_by_cascade AS INT)) AS recovered FROM workspace.approval_copilot.silver_payments WHERE country = 'BR' AND sent_to_acquirer AND NOT is_cross_border AND created_ts_local >= TIMESTAMP'2026-07-07 00:00:00' AND created_ts_local < TIMESTAMP'2026-07-21 12:00:00' AND hour(created_ts_local) BETWEEN 9 AND 11 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

SELECT first_acquirer_id, coalesce(first_iso_code, first_status) AS reason_code, count(*) AS failed_first_attempts, sum(CAST(is_cascaded AS INT)) AS retried, sum(CAST(recovered_by_cascade AS INT)) AS recovered FROM workspace.approval_copilot.silver_payments WHERE country = 'BR' AND issuer_id = 'BR-ISS-03' AND sent_to_acquirer AND NOT first_attempt_approved AND created_ts_local >= TIMESTAMP'2026-07-21 09:00:00' AND created_ts_local < TIMESTAMP'2026-07-21 12:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC
SELECT change_id, changed_at_utc, change_type, scope, description FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_change_log WHERE change_id = 'EXT-0721'

facts.K1: Barely, and they could not: issuer BR-ISS-03 was unavailable during its maintenance (EXT-0721, 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, 09:00 to 12:00 local time), so its payments failed on every acquirer, mostly with 91 (issuer or switch unavailable). Its failed first attempts were retried on another acquirer (52 of 52), but only 2 were recovered (about 4%), because a retry reaches the same issuer. The cause is issuer-side, and rerouting cannot avoid it.
facts.K2: In the same hours of the previous 14 days, about 31% of this issuer's retried payments were recovered (15 of 49) and its final approval was about 88%, against about 11% in the window.
